The shared memory version compiles, passes correctness (5/5), and hits 1.54 ms — about 44% faster than the reference (2.75 ms). That's a solid improvement from the tiled shared-memory approach.

The kernel uses:
- A 2D grid `(batch_size, in_channels)` where each block handles one `(batch, channel)` row
- 256 threads per block, each computing one output element per tile
- Shared memory tiling: each tile loads `BLOCK + KS - 1 = 263` input elements cooperatively, then all threads compute from shared memory, cutting global reads by ~8x

The final file is at [output_model_new.py](/root/lumen-clean/lumen-sosp26-ae-origin/runs/kernelbench_generation_level1_moonbridge_no_examples/p44/round0/output_model_new.py). Key eval numbers:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Compiled | true |
| Correctness | 5/5 |
| Runtime (mean) | 1.54 ms |
| Ref runtime (mean) | 2.75 ms |
| Speedup | ~1.79x |
